title: A study with a new treatment VRN110755 to know the best dose and how well it works, and safety is in people with a specific type of lung cancer (Non-small Cell Lung Cancer) caused by changes (mutations) in the EGFR gene.
official: A Phase 1/2 Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Efficacy of VRN110755 in Patients with Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) Mutant Non-small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC)
summary:
Main objective Part 1a:
To evaluate the safety and tolerability of VRN110755 in patients with EGFR mutant NSCLC.
 To determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of VRN110755 in Phase 1a of the study.
Part 1b: 
To evaluate the safety and tolerability of VRN110755 at the two selected dose levels across the four biomarker- and treatment-line-defined cohorts of patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC.
To determine the recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D) of VRN110755
Phase 2: to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of VRN110755
conditions: Epidermal growth factor receptor gene mutation
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. 1.Patients must be ≥ 18 years of age (≥ 19 years of age for patients in Korea).
2. 10. Phase 1a: • NSCLC with any EGFR activating mutations including Del19, L858R, C797S, and uncommon or complex mutations. • Patients with PD confirmed by radiological evaluation even with standard of care including EGFR TKI treatment for at least 2 cycles; treatment discontinued due to toxicity; and medically confirmed to derive no clinical benefit from other standard therapies.
3. 11. Phase 1b: • Cohort A: NSCLC with Del19 or L858R with C797X EGFR mutations after progression with prior third-generation EGFR TKI as first-line therapy, including osimertinib, lazertinib, or aumolertinib. • Cohort B: NSCLC with common EGFR mutation who are treatment-naïve. • Cohort C: NSCLC with atypical or uncommon EGFR mutation (including G719X, L861Q, S768I, E709X, R776H, L747S, and their combination) who have previously received at least 1 prior systemic therapy, including EGFR TKI, experienced treatment discontinuation due to toxicity, and were medically confirmed to derive no clinical benefit from other standard therapies. • Cohort D: NSCLC with EGFR atypical mutation who are treatment-naïve.
4. 2. Able to comprehend and willing to sign an informed consent form and to abide by the study restrictions.
5. 3. Have at least one measurable extracranial lesion per RECIST Version 1.1, as assessed  by the investigator.
6. 4. Histologically or cytologically confirmed diagnosis of advanced (Stage IIIB not amenable to curative therapy), metastatic (Stage IV), or recurrent NSCLC harboring a documented EGFR mutation, and without evidence of histologic transformation to small cell lung cancer or other neuroendocrine carcinoma. 5.EGFR mutation profile determined by liquid biopsy or pre-existing tumor biopsy result. 6. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0 to 1. 7. Willingness and ability to swallow oral medication and comply with study procedures. 8. Agree to abide by contraception as outlined in the protocol 9.Patients with no appropriate standard treatment options approved in participating countries by investigator’s determination, or standard of treatment options that are not determined to be feasible, per investigator’s decision. 10. Phase 1a: • NSCLC with any EGFR activating mutations including Del19, L858R, C797S, and uncommon or complex mutations. • Patients with PD confirmed by radiological evaluation even with standard of care including EGFR TKI treatment for at least 2 cycles; treatment discontinued due to toxicity; and medically confirmed to derive no clinical benefit from other standard therapies. Phase 1b: • Cohort A: NSCLC with Del19 or L858R with C797X EGFR mutations after progression with prior third-generation EGFR TKI as first-line therapy, including osimertinib, lazertinib, or aumolertinib. • Cohort B: NSCLC with common EGFR mutation who are treatment-naïve. • Cohort C: NSCLC with atypical or uncommon EGFR mutation (including G719X, L861Q, S768I, E709X, R776H, L747S, and their combination) who have previously received at least 1 prior systemic therapy, including EGFR TKI, experienced treatment discontinuation due to toxicity, and were medically confirmed to derive no clinical benefit from other standard therapies. • Cohort D: NSCLC with EGFR atypical mutation who are treatment-naïve.
7. 5.EGFR mutation profile determined by liquid biopsy or pre-existing tumor biopsy result.
8. 6. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0 to 1.
9. 7. Willingness and ability to swallow oral medication and comply with study procedures.
10. 8. Agree to abide by contraception as outlined in the protocol
11. 9.Patients with no appropriate standard treatment options approved in participating countries by investigator’s determination, or standard of treatment options that are not determined to be feasible, per investigator’s decision.
Exclusion criteria:
1. 1.Receipt of any investigational anticancer agent within 14 days or 5 half-lives (whichever is longer) prior to first dose of IMP.
2. 10. Known history or active human immunodeficiency virus infection.
3. 11. Received live vaccines within 4 weeks of the first dose of the IMP
4. 12. Use of known strong or moderate inhibitors/inducers of CYP3A or herbal supplements within 2 weeks of first dose of the IMP.
5. 13.Have had major surgery within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of the IMP.
6. 14. Have received the following anticancer therapy prior to the first dose of IMP:  • For systemic cancer therapy, within 14 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer.  • Antibody or immunotherapy within 28 days.  • Radiotherapy to a large field or including a vital organ within 14 days, or 7 days if vital organ not included.
7. 15.  CNS metastases or spinal cord compression that is associated with progressive neurological symptoms or requires increasing doses of corticosteroids (based on prednisone therapy up to 10 mg daily or equivalent).
8. 16. Medical condition requiring prednisone therapy of more than 10 mg (> 10mg) daily or equivalent systemic steroid therapy.
9. 17. Any of the following heart-related medical history:  • Mean QTcF > 470 msec from 12-lead triplicate electrocardiogram measurements  • Arrhythmic symptoms requiring treatment, symptomatic or uncontrolled atrial fibrillation, or persistent asymptomatic ventricular fibrillation.  • Heart failure at risk of QTc prolongation, hypokalemia, Torsade de Pointes, congenital QT prolongation syndrome, etc.  • Coronary artery bypass graft, vascular stent implantation, myocardial infarction, unstable angina, New York Heart Association Grade 2 or higher congestive heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure > 160 mmHg, diastolic blood pressure > 100 mmHg), or left ventricular ejection fraction < 50% within the last 6 months.  • Use of known QTc prolongation inducing medication within 2 weeks of first dose of the IMP.
10. 18. Patients with a history of (noninfectious) pneumonitis/radiation pneumonitis/interstitial lung disease that required steroids or has current pneumonitis/interstitial lung disease.
11. 19. Unable to swallow capsules or intractable nausea, vomiting, or gastrointestinal diseases that interfere with proper absorption of the drug or absorption disorders that may interfere with absorption of VRN110755.
12. 2.Adverse events from previous chemotherapy that have not recovered to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) Grade ≤ 1 level (≤ Grade 2 peripheral neuropathy or hair loss is acceptable).
13. 20. History of allergy or suspected allergy to the active ingredient of this IMP.
14. 21. Patients who are deemed inappropriate to participate in the study as determined by the investigator.
15. 22. Current or history of alcohol or drug abuse within 2 years of the first dose of the IMP and any current psychological or social condition as determined by the investigator that may affect the participation in the study and evaluation of the results.
16. 23. Use of any acid reducing-agents (ARAs; including PPIs and histamine-2 antagonists) or locally acting antacids within 7 days of the first dose of IMP.
17. 24. Phase 1b and 2: (applicable only to Cohorts A, B, C, and D). Known oncogenic driver alterations with approved therapies, such as: •Amplification: c-MET, HER2  • Fusion: ALK, ROS1, NTRK, RET  • Mutation: BRAF (V600E), KRAS (G12X).
18. 3.Pregnant women, breast-feeding women, or women of childbearing potential who plan to get pregnant.
19. 4. NSCLC confirmed with EGFR/HER2 Exon20 Insertion mutation.
20. 5. History of other active malignancy within 3 years prior to screening
21. 6.Patients the following findings during the screening test:  -Hematology (transfusion or hematopoietic growth factor administration within 14 days prior to test is not allowed)  White blood cell count < 2.5 × 109 /L Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) < 1500/µL Platelets < 100 000/µL Hemoglobin < 9.0 g/dL. -Blood chemistry Creatinine clearance < 60 mL/min according to the Cockroft-Gault equation Total bilirubin > 1.5 × ULN AST (SGOT) > 2.5 × ULN (> 5 × ULN with liver metastases)  ALT (SGPT) > 2.5 × ULN (> 5 × ULN with liver metastases).
22. 7.Active infections (including tuberculosis infection, etc.) requiring systemic antibacterial, antifungal, or antiviral therapy within 14 days prior to first dose of the IMP.
23. 8.Patient has active or chronic hepatitis B at screening.
24. 9.Patient has active or chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV).
